prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup / stylized-concept. Create one bold, art-directed UI concept board for the cozy birdwatching game "Little Elsewhere", direction 20 "Tideglass Atlas". Reference image is only for the geography and subject of the game: looking out from a small balcony, a large tree at left with birds, potted plants and bird food on the sill, an irregular curving river shore with a distant town, layered snowy mountains and sky. Preserve that premise. Completely redesign every interface element; REMOVE the reference's dark debug toolbar and old rectangular interface.
Output a polished landscape 16:9 high-resolution illustration / UI art proposal, ideally 1920x1080. Approx left 70% shows a fully composed game HUD in context, with the landscape's center left open to breathe. Approx right 30% shows a matching open field-guide design with a sparrow study and small collector cards. Both form one coherent art-direction presentation, not a browser page or dashboard.
Art direction: a beautifully hand-engraved nautical naturalist's atlas, pale sea-glass blue and warm ivory paper, deeply inked navy contours, a little aged brass. Bold round compass-rose and tidal dial controls with hand-etched ticks, curling paper chart edges, ropes subtly weaving through the field guide spine, die-cut bird specimen tickets, an irregular pale parchment title cartouche shaped like a small sailing banner. The field guide looks like an open portolan atlas with illustrated bird plates and compass annotations. Strong expressive engraved linework and tactile handmade papers, flat crafted illustration. NO generic rounded rectangles or stock game UI. Big memorable silhouette shapes, playful yet calm and collectable, never ornate muddy excess. Make this clearly distinct from ordinary flat rectangles.
Typography: carefully typeset maritime serif title "Little Elsewhere", short exact labels "Field Guide", "Sparrow", "Observe", "Focus", "12/50"; use only short readable text, not dense placeholder copy. Clear selected/tab states. Palette restrained, no oily painting, no neon, no photorealistic 3D. No watermarks, no exterior presentation border.
